inspection.public_editorial_exposure: After the first native view, web search returned Wikisource pitch encodings and Latin snippets. These are disclosed collation exposure; numeric durations were not taken from them. DIAMM source description and scholarly Latin transcription were consulted. Independence is from producer files, not blindness to public editions.

rule_transcriptions.policy: Expanded Latin reading with abbreviation and minor spelling uncertainty retained separately; not a letter-for-letter diplomatic edition.
rule_transcriptions.boxed: Hanc rotam cantare possunt quatuor socij. A paucioribus autem quam a tribus uel saltem duobus non debet dici, preter eos qui dicunt pedem. Cantatur autem sic. Tacentibus ceteris unus inchoat cum hiis qui tenent pedem. Et cum uenerit ad primam notam post crucem inchoat alius, et sic de ceteris. Singuli uero repausent ad pausaciones scriptas et non alibi, spacio unius longe note.

boxed_uncertainties.issue: Abbreviated verbal form; some public transcriptions expand Canitur. No difference to the retained performance instruction.
Expansion of compact abbreviation; lexical function is legible, exact abbreviation shapes not fully encoded here.

rule_transcriptions.upper_red: Hoc repetit unus quociens opus est, faciens pausacionem in fine.
rule_transcriptions.lower_red: Hoc dicit alius, pausans in medio et non in fine. Set immediate repetens principium.
rule_transcriptions.lower_uncertainty: Set/Sed is an orthographic or abbreviation-expansion alternative. The visible negative before in fine is retained: this is not a pause at both middle and end.

rule_semantics.claim: Four rota companions can sing; fewer than three, or at least two, should not sing, apart from the pes singers.
rule_semantics.qualification: Three/four and a two-singer fallback are the written alternatives. Quatuor possunt is not a proof that five humans or doubling a part is impossible. This receipt does not expand the selected 2-4 rota-singer source family.

rule_semantics.claim: One rota singer begins together with the pes performers while the other rota singers are silent.
When the preceding singer reaches the first note after the cross, another begins; subsequent singers do likewise.
rule_semantics.reason_index_null: Rota melody and cross-to-note indexing are outside this independent subtask.

rule_semantics.claim: Each singer is to pause at written pauses and not elsewhere, for one long note.
rule_semantics.scope_qualification: The boxed instruction's immediate context is the rota singers; assigning precisely this duration to each pes pause additionally treats the prescription as shared with the red pes instructions.

rule_semantics.claim: One performer repeats the upper pes as often as needed, pausing at its end.
The other pauses in the middle of the lower pes, not at its end, and immediately repeats the beginning.

pitch_rest_relation.claim: The retained pitch/rest order is a cyclic block exchange across the two written parts. Equal numeric block durations and exact temporal phase offset are not established here.
pitch_rest_relation.colour_or_voice_swap: Exchanging the two performers together with their complete parts is a naming symmetry. Moving only a pause, while holding the pitch order fixed, is a different rival.
